# the contributor audit: exact finite-knot replacement

PASS after reading candidate a260044e1f85011a in full. The two notation issues noted below have been corrected. This audits exact replacement, not a cap inequality.

On each internal cell the four curvature moments are continuous, their feasible positive-measure class is compact, and the fixed-mass map to the arm is injective into L2. Strict convexity forces a quadratic maximum to be extreme, and the five-disjoint-sets perturbation bounds its support by four. For the minimum, boundary moment data yield a supporting load with nonzero affine coefficient. Interior data admit a normal supporting plane to the convex value function because the moment curve has full affine span. Its first variation gives the required one-sign curvature contact potential. The root contact lemma then gives at most two interior atoms, plus endpoints. Interpolating the attained min/max preserves all linear records and matches the original square integral exactly.

Weighted terminal curvature has finite mass even with infinite final slope. Its kernel tends to zero in L2 as the support point tends to the terminal level. Compactness, continuity, and fixed-mass injectivity survive. The terminal atom is invisible slack that raises the completed top value; it is not an artificial jump retained in the arm. The moment curve has full two-dimensional affine span, giving at most three atoms at the maximum and four at the minimum. Multiplying the dual contact function by R-t yields the same contact lemma on the interior.

The join inequalities have the correct directions, so independent cell replacements remain globally concave and nonincreasing. Internal slope-intersection levels remain exact, while saturated top inequalities persist. All C,K,J and volume records are preserved cellwise, including the separate m=1 formulas. The per-arm zero-slope coarea is R^m/2 and the total is R^m. A nonzero arm coefficient can have an identically zero expression only for an affine arm; it is coefficient nondegeneracy, not literal nonzero load, that the contact lemma requires.

Reconstruction gives a genuine finite-piecewise-affine concave physical profile. Zero outer endpoint heights and top plateaus are expressly allowed. The later signed-arm extension in candidate fe4ccc381e7e406a removes the horizontal-tangent restriction without a projective measure change and has independent Rate and Optimal audits.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
